channel.title: The Global Monitor
channel.description: Global politics and markets, read as one instrument. Analysis of major political developments and what they mean for equities, commodities and currencies.

item.title: The Hormuz Premium: What a Fifth of the World's Oil Is Actually Worth
item.description: Transits fell to three a day and war-risk cover went from 0.125% of hull value to 5%. A framework for pricing chokepoint risk — and why "Iran will close Hormuz" has been a losing forecast all year.

item.title: Record Profits, Record Selloff: What's Actually Happening to Memory Stocks
item.description: SK Hynix posted record profit and had its worst month since 2008. Micron grew revenue 345.7% and trades at 6x forward earnings. The bull and bear cases, and why this one is genuinely unresolved.

item.title: Gold, Silver and Metal Market Volatility
item.description: Gold hit $5,589 in January and gave most of it back by June; silver round-tripped from $121 to $58. Why war and rate cuts moved metals — and why silver moves twice as hard.

item.title: A Trillion Dollars Off the AI Trade
item.description: Chip stocks shed over $1tn this month — yet Samsung's profit rose more than 1,800% and the stock still fell 7%. The market has stopped trading earnings and started trading the multiple.

item.title: Iran's Surprise Strike and the Oil Spike
item.description: Tehran fired a volley of ballistic missiles at US forces in the Gulf hours after traders had started pricing the war out — every missile intercepted, but the risk premium snapped straight back.

item.title: Trump, America, and Tariffs
item.description: The average tariff rate went from 2.4% to 16.8% in a year, revenue jumped 192%, and the Supreme Court just ruled a chunk of it illegal — what the numbers actually say, past the political framing.

item.title: America, Iran, and the Middle East in Chaos
item.description: Operation Epic Fury killed Iran's Supreme Leader within hours of launching and sent oil above $119 a barrel within a week. Five months on, the ceasefire it produced is still fraying.
